title: The Knight's Shortest Trip

concept.title: Squares are nodes and legal moves are edges; BFS counts the moves
body: A chess *knight* moves two squares in one direction and one square in the other, so from the square `(r, c)` it can go to up to **eight** squares: `(r ± 1, c ± 2)` and `(r ± 2, c ± 1)`. What is the smallest number of moves from one square to another on an `n x n` board?

The squares are nodes, a legal move is an edge, and all moves cost the same, so it is the shortest-path problem of the BFS tasks. The only new thing is the list of **eight direction pairs**, and the check that a new square is **on the board**. A two-dimensional distance array filled with -1 serves as the "seen" marker.
On very small boards some squares cannot be reached (on a 3 x 3 board the centre square has no knight moves at all), so the answer can be -1. The time is O(n^2).

statement: A knight stands on the square `(r1, c1)` of an `n x n` chessboard. A move goes two squares in one direction and one square in a perpendicular direction, and must end on the board. Print the smallest number of moves needed to reach the square `(r2, c2)`, or -1 if it cannot be reached.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the size of the board.
The second line has four numbers `r1 c1 r2 c2`: the row and column of the start and of the target square (rows and columns are numbered from 1).
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of moves or -1.

examples.note: From one corner of a normal chessboard to the opposite corner takes 6 moves.
On a 3 x 3 board the knight cannot leave the centre: -1.

hints: The squares are nodes; list the eight moves of the knight.
Run a breadth-first search from the start square, keeping the distance of every square.
Print the distance of the target square (it is -1 if it was never reached).

explanation: A breadth-first search over the squares using the eight knight moves gives the smallest number of moves to every reachable square; the target is read from the distance table.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a, b, c, d = map(int, input().split())

moves = [(1, 2), (2, 1), (-1, 2), (-2, 1), (1, -2), (2, -1), (-1, -2), (-2, -1)]
dist = [[-1] * n for _ in range(n)]
dist[a - 1][b - 1] = 0
queue = [(a - 1, b - 1)]
for x, y in queue:
    for dx, dy in moves:
        p, q = x + dx, y + dy
        if 0 <= p < n and 0 <= q < n and dist[p][q] < 0:
            dist[p][q] = dist[x][y] + 1
            queue.append((p, q))
print(dist[c - 1][d - 1])
